questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is false?
options: Protons are found in the nucleus and are positively charged.
Electrons move around the nucleus and contribute little mass to the atom.
Neutrons are found in the nucleus and have no charge.
The numbers of neutrons, protons and electrons are always equal in an atom.
questions.explanation: D. The numbers of neutrons, protons and electrons are always equal in an atom.. [1]

questions.prompt: An atom has 21 protons, 22 neutrons and 18 electrons. It is
The Mass Number of an atom is equal to
options: the number of protons plus neutrons.
the number of protons plus neutrons plus electrons.
the average mass of atoms of one element.
questions.explanation: B. the number of protons plus neutrons.. [1]

questions.prompt: Which statement is false about an atom of hydrogen?
options: It has one proton, one neutron and one electron.
It has an atomic number of 1.
It has a mass number of 1.
It has an atomic mass of approximately 1.
questions.explanation: A. It has one proton, one neutron and one electron.. [1]

questions.prompt: Which of the following has the most electrons in its outer shell?
questions.explanation: Learning Vault created — corrected key: C, Carbon. Carbon has four outer-shell electrons, whereas helium has two, lithium one, and zinc two in its outermost shell. The supplied key D is retained in source metadata.

questions.prompt: On the Periodic Table, the group that an element is found in tells you
options: the number of protons in its nucleus.
the number of shells that contain electrons.
the number of electrons in the outer shell.
the number of neutrons in the nucleus.
questions.explanation: C. the number of electrons in the outer shell.. [1]

questions.prompt: Which scientist contributed towards the arrangement of the modern Periodic Table
The Noble gases are all found in the last group of the periodic table because
options: they all have full electron shells.
questions.explanation: D. they all have full electron shells.. [1]

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about a neutral atom of magnesium?
options: It has an electron configuration of 2, 8, 12.
questions.explanation: C. It has 2 valence (outer shell) electrons.. [1]

questions.prompt: Elements are arranged on the Periodic Table in order of

Isotopes are atoms with
options: the same number of protons but different numbers of electrons.
the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons.
the same number of electrons but different numbers of neutrons.
questions.explanation: B. the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.. [1]

questions.prompt: Which is the correct order from smallest to largest?
The Big Bang Theory describes the origin of the universe as ‘singularity’. Singularity consisted of
The first fundamental interaction in the universe was
Which of the following was true about the expanding universe?
options: Its average temperature has been increasing.
Its average density has been decreasing.
The amount of energy has been increasing.
The amount of matter has been decreasing.
questions.explanation: B. Its average density has been decreasing.. [1]

questions.prompt: Which of the following is true about the Big Bang Theory?
options: Galaxies are moving apart from each other as the universe expands.
Stars are being thrown apart from each other due to the momentum of a past explosion.
The universe suddenly appeared in space.
The Big Bang attempts to explain why the universe was created, what existed before the universe and what exists outside of the universe.
questions.explanation: A. Galaxies are moving apart from each other as the universe expands.. [1]

questions.prompt: Which is the correct sequence of events?
options: formation of stars, formation of galaxies, formation of matter, formation of solar systems, humans appeared on Earth
formation of galaxies, formation of stars, formation of matter, formation of solar systems, humans appeared on Earth
formation of matter, formation of stars, formation of galaxies, formation of solar systems, humans appeared on Earth
formation of solar systems, humans appeared on Earth, formation of stars, formation of galaxies, formation of matter
questions.explanation: C. formation of matter, formation of stars, formation of galaxies, formation of solar systems, humans appeared on Earth. [1]

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not evidence for the Big Bang Theory?
options: The universe continues to expand, as measured using Doppler Effect and spectral shift analysis.
There is an abundance of hydrogen and helium, the first two elements to exist in the universe, at levels predicted by Big Bang Theorists.
Cosmic microwave radiation exists uniformly in the universe as background radiation, at levels predicted by the Big Bang theorists.
The Square Kilometre Array has detected hadrons and measured gravity waves which show the existence of black holes, as predicted by Big Bang Theorists.
questions.explanation: D. The Square Kilometre Array has detected hadrons and measured gravity waves which show the existence of black holes, as predicted by Big Bang Theorists.. [1]

questions.prompt: In spectral analysis of stars, red shift occurs
options: as a star moves towards us.

questions.prompt: The source of energy for our star is
options: nuclear fission of helium to form hydrogen.
nuclear fusion of hydrogen to form helium
nucleosynthesis of protons and neutrons to form hydrogen
questions.explanation: B. nuclear fusion of hydrogen to form helium. [1]

questions.prompt: Our sun is a medium star. It will become all of the following during its lifetime, except a
Which is the correct sequence for the life cycle a very large star
options: Stellar nebula  massive star  red hypergiant  supernova  black hole
Planetary nebula  White dwarf  red hypergiant  supernova  Pulsar
Stellar nebula  massive star  red hypergiant  supernova  Planetary nebula
Stellar nebula  massive star  blue ghost giant  supernova  black hole
questions.explanation: A. Stellar nebula  massive star  red hypergiant  supernova  black hole. [1]

questions.prompt: The Large Hadron Collider was built by CERN, the European Organisation for Nuclear Research, between 1998 and 2008, at a cost of US$6 billion, to allow physicists to test their predictions of different theories of particle physics and search for new particles as predicted by supersymmetry, one of several new theories to evolve from Big Bang Theory and the Standard Model. Which of the following statements about the Large Hadron Collider is true?
options: It is the largest machine in the world.
It orbits approximately 400 km above the Earth at a speed of 27,600 km/hr.
It has been running continuously since 2008.
questions.explanation: B. It is the largest machine in the world.. [1]
